terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. The most common vehicle on Thai roads. The plate shows a navy underbone with white pinstripes on the leg shield and side covers, a black vinyl seat, a chrome rear rack with a slotted plate, round chrome mirrors on tall stems, a rectangular headlamp between amber indicators, silver engine cases with a forward-canted barrel, a chain to a rear sprocket, a dusty exhaust on the right and wire-spoked wheels with drum hubs.

reasoning: The identity is the underbone layout: a leg shield rising to a handlebar cowl, a step-through floor, side covers under a flat seat, a chrome rack behind it, wire-spoked wheels front and rear. It is an assembly of small parts, not one shell.

Three materials: the paint (leg shield, covers, seat, fenders, cowl, swingarm, fork shrouds, pinstripes as vertex colours), a white vertex-coloured trim carrying chrome, alloy, lamps and black rubber, and a third for the tyres, whose tread tile has to multiply the rubber without touching anything else.
One repetition system: two wheels off one open wire-wheel geometry, each a named pivot on its axle.
Action readiness is the wheels: two hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable. Steering is not articulated.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A motorcycle is legible by its silhouette gaps as much as its masses -- the step-through, the daylight under the seat, the space inside the fork, and above all the daylight THROUGH a wire wheel -- so the frame is tubes, the panels are thin extrusions, and the wheel is an open tyre ring with a rim, a drum hub and eighteen prism spokes rather than a dished disc.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The wheels are wire-spoked in the plate and are built OPEN: a closed tyre-ring lathe, a rim ring, a drum hub and eighteen three-sided prism spokes, with daylight through them. The first build used the closed dished lathe, which is a solid disc that HIDES the spokes merged into it -- it shipped two grey discs.

The turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires on the step-through gap, the daylight inside the fork, under the seat and now through the wire wheels: real open air on a motorcycle. --allow-holes is set on the _holecc measurement.
The right side is mirrored from the left; the exhaust runs on the right, dull and dusty rather than bright chrome (measured #4d4137 on the plate's silencer).
The chain, sprockets and kickstart are read off the plate's left-side crop; the countershaft sprocket is inferred behind its cover at confidence 0.75.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.71 x 1.25 x 1.92 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=8 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (2); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: Wheels 0.556 m in diameter at z +0.64 and -0.58 (1.22 wheelbase); a front fender hugging the tyre at 18-38 mm from -8 to 134 degrees; chrome fork sliders on 27 degrees of rake THROUGH the front hub, into navy shrouds and a triple clamp at 0.83; a handlebar cowl 0.87-1.015 m carrying a rectangular headlamp and two amber pods; bars at 1.00 m across 0.69 m with mirrors to 1.258 m; a leg shield from 0.30 to 0.87 m, front face z +0.575, top edge back at z +0.30; a step-through floor at 0.28-0.32 m; side covers 0.47-0.672 m from z +0.08 to -0.47 under a seat at 0.674-0.755 m from z +0.11 to -0.46; a chrome rack 0.75 m over z -0.46..-0.93; engine 0.19-0.46 m between the wheels with the barrel canted 20 degrees forward.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.356..+0.356 at the mirror heads; y 0.000 to 1.258 at the mirror tips; z -0.939 to +0.942, rear mudflap to front fender, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy (bbox 1.897 x 1.240 x 0.727) normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.654 : 0.383, i.e. 1.92 x 1.255 x 0.735 at the declared length, and the wheel centres sit at 0.15 L and 0.80 L for a 1.23 m wheelbase. The registry height of 1.07 was a list-time estimate to the BAR TOPS; it has been corrected to 1.25 on the proxy arithmetic, with the bars still at 1.00 and the mirrors carrying the rest.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.654 : 0.383. Its side elevation and occupancy map (scratch/honda-wave/_ev/) read wheel centres at 0.15 L and 0.80 L, bars at 0.80 H, mirror tips at 0.98 H, seat top at 0.60 H over 0.50-0.73 L, rack at 0.545 H over 0.75-0.98 L and the leg shield spanning 0.21-0.35 L -- and those fractions at the declared 1.92 m are what is built. The first build read the same map at a wrong length and put the front axle 0.12 m too far back.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.80: the plate shows the left side; the right is mirrored, with the exhaust on the right as the type has it.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-paint (side cover, PBR confidence 0.763) at #343f58, luma 63 -- the plate reads #2b3551 lit and #1e2638 in shade, and #343f58 is the mid. textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components and one repetition system: 3 of 8. Sixty-odd fittings ride one merge.

materials.note: paint, a white vertex-coloured trim and a rubber carrying the tread tile: 3 of 4. Chrome, alloy, vinyl and lamps differ in albedo only and share the trim; the tyre is separate ONLY because its canvas would otherwise multiply them.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,716 of 4,000: the open wire wheel is the cost at ~600 triangles per geometry (two instances), and every tube run whose ends are buried is built open, which is half the triangles of a capped one.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Thin side-profile extrusions for the panels and the tyre-hugging fenders, polyline tubes for the frame, drivetrain and fittings, lathes for the lamp pods and engine covers, an open wire-wheel lathe, boxes for the rest.
One InstancedMesh carries both wheels. No per-instance colour.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. Two canvases are bound after construction: a 256 px dust multiplier on the paint and a 256 px tread on the rubber. 0.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory 85 ms.

risks.description: The turntable gate flags the step-through, the fork daylight and now the gaps between the spokes.
risks.mitigation: Real open air on a motorcycle; --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement logged per azimuth.

3,716 of 4,000 leaves 7 percent of headroom; a third wheel or a rider would not fit.
